name: recording-device-login-own-prompt

graded_by.test: core/internal/record/login_write_test.go — TestADeviceLoginWritesTSBsOwnPromptsAsCode8: code 8 `login as:` before the user name's code 7, and code 8 `Password:` before a password round's code 7, in exactly the x-own-prompt-line bytes

description: TSB's own prompt text on disk, sidecar code 8, in a device login's head. With policy.yaml recording.login_input on, `recording.enabled` on and `recording_acknowledged` true on the create, the head holds: (1) code 8, the fixed line `login as:`, then code 7, the user name typed at it; (2) a keyboard-interactive round as before, code 6 for the text the device sent and code 7 for the answer; (3) for a password round, code 8, the fixed line `Password:`, then code 7, the answer. Code 6 stays text the device sent and code 7 the answers, so a code-6 line never carries TSB's words, and the device's own `Password:` (code 6) cannot pass as TSB's (code 8). Code 8 carries no secret. It is written only where the login frames are, and a supplied login, which is never asked at a prompt, has none. Refused: a code-8 line with any other text or another tag, and a code-8 frame after the session's first output frame. The answers are the synthetic constant.

invalid.note: code 8 holds one of two fixed lines, `login as:` and `Password:`; any other text is refused
code 8 carries its own tag, not the answer tag
a code-8 frame after the session's first output frame: the own-prompt lines are the head of the recording
